provides: User authentication and account access: sign-up and sign-in with email or phone one-time codes, passwords, social (OAuth) accounts, corporate SSO (SAML/OIDC), magic links, QR hand-off and passkeys; guest (anonymous) access; two-factor authentication and step-up verification; session and device management with a security audit trail.

curated.summary: Visitors get a temporary anonymous account (e.g. to browse or fill a cart) that can later be upgraded to a full account; guest data merges on upgrade.
Users can protect their account with time-based one-time codes (Google Authenticator etc.); also the factor behind step-up checks on sensitive actions.
curated.business_label: Two-factor authentication with an authenticator app

curated.summary: New users can create an account by confirming their phone number with a one-time SMS code.
New users can create an account by confirming their email with a one-time code.
New users can create an account through Google, GitHub, Apple and other configured OAuth providers.
Employees signing in through their company identity provider (SAML/OIDC) get an account provisioned on first login.
curated.business_label: Automatic accounts for corporate SSO users

curated.summary: New users can register with a login and password. Off by default — passwordless methods are the house default.

How the sign-in-by-code screens answer somebody whose address has no account while sign-up is off. 'silent' (default) answers everyone identically and simply never sends the stranger a code — nobody can probe the endpoint to learn who works here, at the price that a mistyped address waits for a letter that will not come. 'request' says 'sign-up is closed' immediately, which is the friendliest message and also lets anyone enumerate your member list. 'verify' still sends the code and refuses at the last step — enumerable AND it mails strangers.
curated.business_label: What a stranger sees when sign-up is closed

curated.summary: When a sign-up request carries the advertising click identifier the visitor arrived on, store it against the new account. Nothing is collected here on its own: a row exists only if your own front end sends it, which the shipped capture code does only after the visitor accepted analytics. It is what later lets you report a real conversion — the account that started paying weeks after it registered — back to the ad platform, which is impossible from the browser alone. Switch it off and the field is ignored rather than refused, so an already-deployed front end keeps registering people.
curated.business_label: Remember which ad a new account came from

curated.summary: When on, setting a password on a guest session turns it into a full registered account (login/password IS the identity). Off by default — a password is normally just a credential that makes a guest account portable, and only a verified anchor (email/phone/social) registers.
curated.business_label: A password counts as signing up (90s-style accounts)

curated.summary: Existing users sign in by receiving a one-time SMS code.
Existing users sign in by receiving a one-time code by email.
Existing users sign in through the configured OAuth providers.
Users of onboarded organizations sign in through their company identity provider (SAML/OIDC), configured per organization in the database.
Existing users sign in with login and password (plus change/reset flows). Off by default.
A signed-in device shows a QR code; scanning it signs the user in on the new device.
curated.business_label: Sign-in by QR code from another device

curated.summary: Users sign in with platform passkeys (Face ID, fingerprint, hardware security keys) via WebAuthn; also usable as a second factor.
Users sign in by clicking a short-lived link sent to their email — no code entry.
curated.business_label: Sign-in via a one-time email link

gates.behavior: When on, POST /grant/exchange/ trades a token minted by the auth.issue_login_grant comm function for a JWT session; a grant minted with create_if_missing provisions an email account with a verified address and no usable password.

curated.summary: Trusted modules (e.g. the workspaces invite flow) mint a short-lived single-use grant token through an internal call; exchanging it signs the user in and can auto-create a verified account. Off by default.
curated.business_label: Sign-in via a service-issued login grant

gates.behavior: When on (and AUTH_PASSWORD_LOGIN is on too), POST /token/ trades username-or-email plus password for a JWT pair, under the same lockout and the same TOTP step-up as POST /password/login/. When off it answers 403.

curated.summary: Deprecated alias of password sign-in for clients pinned to the old token-pair response. Off by default; needs password sign-in on as well.
curated.business_label: Sign-in through the legacy token endpoint

curated.summary: Controls whether the email one-time-code method renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
curated.business_label: Where the email sign-in method appears

curated.summary: Controls whether the phone one-time-code method renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
curated.business_label: Where the phone sign-in method appears

curated.summary: Controls whether password sign-in renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
curated.business_label: Where the password sign-in method appears

curated.summary: Controls whether the one-time email-link method renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
curated.business_label: Where the email-link sign-in method appears

curated.summary: Controls whether corporate SSO renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
Controls whether social (OAuth) sign-in renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
Controls whether QR hand-off sign-in renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.
Controls whether passkey sign-in renders inline in the primary sign-in tabs, behind the "more" menu, or in the bottom button row. Purely presentational.

gates.behavior: When on, a successful OAuth login with a TOTP-enrolled account returns a TOTP challenge instead of tokens.

curated.summary: Require a two-factor code even after a social (OAuth) login. Off by default — the provider already authenticated the user.

gates.behavior: When on, a successful password login with a TOTP-enrolled account returns a TOTP challenge instead of tokens.

curated.summary: Require a two-factor code after password login for TOTP-enrolled accounts. On by default — a password alone is phishable.

extension_points.name: OAUTH_PROVIDER_CLASSES
extension_points.summary: Register additional OAuth providers (subclass stapel_core.oauth.OAuthProvider in the host app, append the dotted path) — no fork.

extension_points.name: REREGISTRATION_MODEL
extension_points.summary: Swap the model that stores re-registration hashes; resolved lazily, stapel-gdpr is not a hard dependency.

extension_points.name: AUTH_USER_MODEL
extension_points.summary: Standard Django user swap — subclass stapel-core's AbstractStapelUser; this module only ever uses get_user_model().

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every user-facing view declares *_request/_response_serializer_class seams (SerializerSeamsMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, mount via the URL factories.

extension_points.name: STAPEL_VERIFICATION.EXTRA_FACTORS
extension_points.summary: Add step-up verification factors to the stapel-core registry alongside the built-ins this module registers (otp_email, otp_phone, totp, passkey).

extension_points.name: url_factories
extension_points.summary: Compose your own URLconf from the get_*_urls() factories so disabled features 404 (include('stapel_auth.urls') mounts everything with per-request gating).

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.email_mock
surface.intent: Published SO THAT a host frontend can render a dev-mode badge: email OTP delivery is mocked here, the code lands in the logs. Same obligation as on the registration DTO — ignoring it turns a dev deployment into a silent dead end for the user.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.oauth
surface.intent: The OAuth providers configured for sign-in, id + display name — render the social buttons from this list.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.passkey
surface.intent: Passkey/WebAuthn sign-in is enabled; gate the platform-authenticator prompt on this in addition to the browser's own capability check.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.password
surface.intent: Password sign-in is enabled. A passwordless deployment must not render a password field.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.phone
surface.intent: Phone OTP sign-in is enabled — drive the sign-in form's method tabs from this, not from a build-time flag.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.phone_mock
surface.intent: Same promise as `email_mock` for phone/SMS OTP delivery, and the same obligation on the consumer.

surface.name: LoginCapabilities.qr
surface.intent: QR hand-off sign-in (scan on a signed-in device to sign in here) is enabled — show the QR affordance only when true.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.anonymous
surface.intent: Guest (anonymous) sign-up is enabled, i.e. the product may let a visitor act before registering. Note the pairing with stapel-core's IsNotAnonymousUser: when this is on, the backend's write endpoints need that permission class rather than a bare IsAuthenticated.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.email
surface.intent: Email OTP sign-up is enabled — same rule as `phone`: the sign-up form's method tabs are deployment state, not build state.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.email_mock
surface.intent: Published SO THAT a host frontend can render a dev-mode badge: email OTP delivery is mocked here and the code goes to the logs instead of an inbox. It does not disable `email` — the channel is on, it just does not deliver. A frontend that ignores this field tells the user 'code sent' when nothing was sent, which is the exact failure this field was published to prevent; it is currently ignored by @stapel/auth-react (#141).

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.oauth
surface.intent: The OAuth providers actually configured here, id + display name. Render the social buttons from this list — a hardcoded Google button in a deployment without Google credentials is a button that always errors.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.password
surface.intent: Password sign-up is enabled. A deployment can be passwordless; a form that always shows a password field on sign-up is showing a field the backend will reject.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.phone
surface.intent: Phone OTP sign-up is enabled in this deployment — render (or hide) the phone tab of the sign-up form from this, never from a build-time flag: the same frontend bundle serves deployments that differ on it.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.phone_mock
surface.intent: Same promise as `email_mock` for phone/SMS OTP delivery, and the same obligation on the consumer.

surface.name: RegistrationCapabilities.sso
surface.intent: Corporate SSO/SAML just-in-time provisioning is enabled — show the 'sign in with your company account' entry point only when this is true.
